hints.title: In-Place Marker State Obstacle
hints.text: Setting rows and columns to zero immediately upon encountering a zero causes newly created zeroes to erroneously trigger further row and column wipes. How can first row and column serve as status markers?

hints.title: First Row Column Marker Invariant
hints.text: Use matrix[0][c] and matrix[r][0] to store whether column c or row r contains a zero, using two separate boolean flags for whether row 0 and column 0 originally contained zero.

hints.title: Two-Pass Zero Propagation Procedure
hints.text: Determine if row 0 or col 0 contains 0. Scan the inner subgrid (1..m-1, 1..n-1); if matrix[r][c] == 0, mark matrix[r][0] = 0 and matrix[0][c] = 0. In a second pass over inner cells, set matrix[r][c] = 0 if its row or col marker is 0. Finally zero out row 0 and col 0 if flagged.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Two passes over the matrix using the first row and column as storage for O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Creating duplicate row and column marker arrays consumes O(M + N) extra space.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Reusing matrix headers achieves constant auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Using two boolean flags for row 0 and column 0 to prevent marker overwrite.
